From 1966 to 1996 France tested nuclear weapons at Moruroa and Fangataufa atolls in French Polynesia, first in the open air and from 1975 underground. Almost 200 tests were fired.

France moved its tests here after Algeria became independent. The test centre brought soldiers, money and jobs to Tahiti, drawing people from the outer islands to Papeete. Fallout reached inhabited islands; France admitted health effects only decades later.

Protests grew across the Pacific. French agents sank the Greenpeace ship Rainbow Warrior in 1985, and a last series of tests in 1995 set off riots in Papeete. Compare the US tests at Bikini.
